summary: Maria from Acme Watches describes a growing brand infringement problem with 340 cases last quarter. Her team manually processes infringements via spreadsheet exports taking 2+ hours weekly. Budget exists ($2000/mo) pending ROI proof. She committed to providing a sample dataset by Friday and an intro to her VP.

top_pains.pain: Manual infringement review is unsustainable and caused analyst attrition
Growing case volume (180→340/quarter) overwhelming small team

commitments.what: Provide sample dataset by Friday for pilot
commitments.next_step: Follow up Thursday if not received

commitments.what: Send intro email to VP Sarah Chen this afternoon
commitments.next_step: Prepare VP-level pitch focusing on ROI

good_questions: Asked about current process (how they handle brand monitoring)
Followed up on specifics (what happens next, two hours getting worse)
Asked what they've tried (speed things up, $3000 tool)

violations.better: Instead of suggesting a pilot, ask what a successful solution would look like to them

suggested_followups: Prepare for VP Sarah Chen meeting - focus on 10+ hours/week savings proof
Quantify the cost of the analyst who quit
open_questions: What does their legal team's capacity look like?
How do they prioritize which infringements to pursue?
What platforms beyond Amazon are problematic?
